passageText:
SuperEditor Import Format - Complete Example

This passage demonstrates all available SuperEditor custom tags that can be used when importing questions. Use this as a reference guide for creating your own import files.

All tags are case-sensitive. Make sure to use exact capitalization: Heading, KeyConcept, Equation, etc.1. Heading Tags

Headings can be used to structure your content hierarchically. Available levels: 1-6.

Main Title Subsection2. KeyConcept Tags

Use KeyConcept to highlight important information. Available styles:

Standard key concept boxCritical informationEmphasized contentCaution or warningDeep insight or tipFormal definitionLearning objectiveAdditional information3. StyledList with ListItem

Create colorful bullet points to organize information:

Blue – General informationGreen – Positive or correct itemsYellow – Important notesOrange – Warnings or attentionRed – Critical or incorrect itemsPurple – Special casesTeal – Alternative approachesPink – Examples or demonstrations4. Table Tags

Tables support three styles: bordered, striped, and borderless. Set hasHeader="true" to make the first row a header.

StyleDescriptionBest ForborderedClear cell bordersStructured datastripedAlternating row colorsLong data listsborderlessNo visible bordersSimple comparisons
5. Equation Tags

Support inline and display math using LaTeX syntax:

Inline: Use <Equation type="inline"> for math within text, like E = mc^2 or \sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}.Display: Use <Equation type="display"> for centered, standalone equations.

Example quadratic formula:

x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}

Multiline equations using \\ for line breaks:

\begin{cases}x + y = 10 \\2x - y = 5\end{cases}6. CardGrid with Card

Create responsive card layouts with 1-4 columns. Available themes: blue, green, purple, orange, teal, pink, indigo, amber.

Understand the problemPlan your approachExecute and verify7. CodeBlock Tags

Display code with syntax highlighting. Supports 30+ languages:

def fibonacci(n): if n <= 1: return n return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2) print(fibonacci(10))const factorial = (n) => { return n <= 1 ? 1 : n * factorial(n - 1); }; console.log(factorial(5)); // 120With these tags, you can create rich, engaging educational content that enhances student understanding!

questionText: Which SuperEditor tag should you use to display a mathematical equation centered on its own line?
explanation:
Answer Explanation

The SuperEditor supports two types of equation display modes:

TypeTagUsageInline<Equation type="inline">Math within text flowDisplay<Equation type="display">Centered, standalone equation
Use <Equation type="display"> for equations that should appear on their own line, centered and prominent.

Example:

\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}

This renders as:

\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}

questionText: You want to create a comparison table with 3 columns showing different approaches. Which combination of tags is correct?
explanation:
Table Structure in SuperEditor

The correct structure for tables in SuperEditor uses three nested components:

<Table> – Container with style and hasHeader attributes<Row> – Each row of the table<Cell> – Individual cells within each rowTable syntax: <Table style="bordered|striped|borderless" hasHeader="true|false">

Complete example:

Approach 1 Approach 2 Approach 3 Fast Memory efficient Easiest to understand

This renders as:

Approach 1Approach 2Approach 3Fast executionMemory efficientEasy to understandComplex codeSlower runtimeHigher memory usage

questionText: How many columns can a CardGrid display at maximum?
explanation:
CardGrid Column Options

CardGrid supports 1 to 4 columns for responsive layouts:

Full width cardsSide-by-side comparisonBalanced grid layoutMaximum densityThe columns attribute can be set to 1, 2, 3, or 4. Choose based on content density and readability.

Example syntax:

Content 1 Content 2 Content 3 Content 4
